summary.intent: Manage a GSD (Get-Shit-Done) milestone dashboard for the cipher-box repo across an overnight/multi-session workflow: verify Phase 70.1, fix a false 'executing' status on Phase 69, discuss and background-plan Phases 74/75/77, resume after multiple quota-limit interruptions, execute those planned phases, and finally ship Phase 74 through the full verify/secure/validate/simplify/SDK-E2E/CodeRabbit/PR pipeline.
summary.outcome: Phases 69, 70.1, 75, and 77 were completed and merged/verified; Phase 74 was planned, executed, and shipped as PR #607 but its ship-phase run surfaced a real runtime bug (base64/hex encoding mismatch in grant re-mint) and a crash-resume security gap, which triggered a TDD gap-closure fix agent still in progress at session end; a hex/base64 wire-encoding hardening task was logged as a follow-up todo.

repo: GSD's plan-file scanner (plan-scan.cjs:28) has a loose /PLAN/i substring fallback that miscounts any .md file containing 'PLAN' (e.g. '69-WRITE-PLANE-RESEARCH.md' due to 'PLANE') as an extra plan file, causing implementation_complete to read false and the dashboard to falsely show 'Executing'.
manager's is_active flag is purely 'a file in the phase dir was modified in the last 5 minutes' — not an indicator of a real running agent.

Share API wire fields (encryptedReadKey, encryptedWriteKey, itemNameEncrypted, sharerPublicKey) are validated as HEX by all 4 DTOs (create-share, create-invite, claim-invite, update-grant) via @Matches(/^(?:[0-9a-fA-F]{2})+$/), while internal node-codec/stored sealed refs (readKeySealed, read_sealed, persist_wrapped_key) use BASE64 — same Uint8Array/string type on both sides with nothing at the type level forcing the correct encoding, so this class of bug has recurred multiple times.

Phase 74's re-mint at engine.rs:617 used base64_encode for encryptedReadKey when the share-grant wire contract requires hex — this passed all mocked unit tests and only surfaced via the live desktop-e2e Windows leg.
EnterWorktree cannot pin a sub-agent launched at the repo root into a pre-existing worktree ('repo root, not an isolated worktree') — confirms and reinforces the prior known limitation.
vitest does not load .env files, so SDK_E2E_SECRET must be explicitly exported before running sdk-e2e suites or the harness falls back to a default secret and gets 401s.
Desktop E2E is dispatch-gated (must be triggered via workflow_dispatch), not automatically run on PR open.
gh pr edit fails on this repo (Projects-classic GraphQL) — must patch PR body via `gh api -X PATCH repos/FSM1/cipher-box/pulls/<N> -F body=@file`.
PR titles and commit subjects must be conventional with no parentheses (commitlint + lint-pr-title CI reject parens).

code.finding: SentShareResponse doc comments mislabeled base64-encoded encrypted_read_key/encrypted_write_key fields as 'Hex-encoded' — genuine doc/code encoding mismatch flagged by crypto review.

re_mint_grants_rooted_at base64-encodes the wrapped read key for the share-grant wire field, but the API's update_grant DTO validates encryptedReadKey as hex — causes a 400 at runtime, only caught by live desktop-e2e, not by mocked unit tests.

TS rotatedNodes map stores the same Uint8Array reference (not a defensive copy) that is also aliased into ParentTrackingState.parentNewReadKey; currently safe because no code zeros parentNewReadKey, but is a latent data-loss/zeroization hazard if that changes — Rust's equivalent map uses .clone() and is safe.
is_active in manager dashboard state is computed as 'file modified in phase dir within last 5 minutes', unrelated to whether an agent is actually running.

workflow: When a background agent dies mid-task due to a session/quota limit, its worktree/branch may still have partial committed work (research/patterns/some plans) even though the task-notification says 'failed' — always assess disk state directly rather than trusting the notification summary before deciding to re-run from scratch.

Scheduling a resume via CronCreate for the next quota reset, and updating/replacing that cron when the recovery strategy changes (e.g. abandoning worktree-based resume for sequential main-checkout-per-branch), is an effective pattern for surviving multi-hour quota-limited autonomous runs.

Sequential processing on the main checkout (switching branches per phase) is more robust than parallel worktree agents when sub-agents can't EnterWorktree from repo root — this became the standing corrected approach mid-session.

A full ship-phase pipeline (verify→secure→validate→simplify→SDK-E2E→CodeRabbit→ship→resolve-reviews→learnings) can pass every local/CI gate yet still have the live E2E/desktop-e2e leg catch a genuine runtime defect that all mocked unit tests missed — the integration gate is not redundant with unit CI.

Delegating heavy audit/analysis stages (secure, crypto-privacy review, security review, simplify) to a self-contained sub-agent while reserving the shared dev stack for the SDK-E2E gate avoids resource contention between analysis and integration testing.
Committing/pushing work-in-progress plan drafts before relaunching a stalled agent (rather than discarding and restarting) preserves partial progress across quota interruptions.

friction: Multiple session/quota limit interruptions ('You've hit your session limit') killed 3 background planners and later a Phase 77 planner/executor mid-run, requiring manual disk-state reassessment and relaunch each time.
EnterWorktree failed for sub-agents launched at repo root trying to pin into pre-existing worktrees, wasting two agent invocations before pivoting to sequential main-checkout-per-branch.

A Phase 75 'Finish and execute' agent silently stopped early after ~21 minutes due to a flawed self-made background-wait loop rather than quota exhaustion, requiring relaunch with explicit instructions not to background-wait.
CodeRabbit's plan-checker agent (with Bash) mutated 75-VALIDATION.md out-of-band mid-run, causing a subsequent plan-checker pass to report a false-positive blocker describing the pre-fix state.
GSD's commit helper repeatedly false-negatived commit_failed while commits actually landed, requiring manual git log verification instead of blind retries.
Pre-commit hooks are slow (~1-2 min due to lint-staged in the monorepo), which was initially mistaken for a possible commit hang/signing block.
The stale dist-based API process on :3000 (running old TEST_LOGIN_SECRET) caused false 401 test failures, requiring restart from source — a recurring known trap noted in project memory.
The hex/base64 encoding bug recurred yet again despite prior awareness, indicating the underlying architectural gap (no type-level enforcement of wire encoding) was never actually closed.
open_items: Phase 74 gap-closure fix agent was still running at session end for 3 defects: (1) SC#2 grant re-mint base64→hex encoding fix, (2) dirty-resume rotatedNodes crash-resume security gap in both Rust and TS engines, (3) desktop-e2e Carol-retained assertion using a stale pre-rotation folder ref — needs re-verification (cargo/typecheck/vitest + desktop-e2e Windows leg) once done.

Todo logged: hex/base64 wire-encoding domain hardening (severity high) — authoritative encoding table doc, named boundary codecs, branded types, and a client↔DTO contract test, to be run as its own hardening phase after Phase 74 merges.
Todo logged: re-mint trusts untrusted server for recipient-pubkey binding (MEDIUM, newly reachable on desktop) — deferred.
Todo logged: TS rotatedNodes defensive-copy parity with Rust's .clone() — deferred as latent hazard.

Server DTO doc-comment mislabels (share-response.dto.ts) for encryptedReadKey/encryptedWriteKey still say 'Hex-encoded' but are base64 — requires pnpm api:generate + regenerated client commit, out of Phase 74 file scope.
Phases 76, 78, 79 remain fully unplanned (76's branch was created then deleted after being stopped by user with zero work done).

Phase 74 PR #607 still has two CI-gated legs to fully confirm post-fix: Cargo Check & Test (Windows) previously passed but needs re-run after gap-closure changes; Desktop E2E Windows leg failed and needs a clean re-run once the encoding fix lands.
User explicitly paused the autonomous cascade before Phase 76/78/79 and has not yet given direction to resume them.
